summary: Rate policy shadowing between tenant-level and per-route enforcement causing repeat 429s for mixed-traffic API key
description:
Issue summary:
The customer reports sustained 429s originating from a mix of short chat sessions (low token per request) and intermittent large batched embedding uploads. Symptoms appear after tenant-level quota increase and a per-route burst window change performed by Veridian Analytics engineering.

Impact:
- Customer production traffic (dedicated pool) experiencing ~3-7% 429 rate across traffic spikes, causing user-facing failures in their ingestion pipeline and chat timeouts.
- Billing and token accounting look anomalous (spike in accounted tokens vs expected).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (redwood-dedicated-12), prod us-east-1
- Customer API key: redacted (sent via secure channel)
- Mixed HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 clients behind a shared gateway at customer side

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start ~250 short-lived chat sessions (few tokens) over 30s while concurrently running 6 parallel batched embedding uploads (multipart) each ~12k tokens.
2) Observe intermittent 429s, mostly for the short chat requests but sometimes for batch jobs.
3) Reduce concurrency to 60 chat sessions and 2 batch upload lanes → errors drop to <0.5%.

Observed logs/headers (snippets):
- 429 responses include X-RateLimit-Reason: tenant_quota_exhausted and X-RateLimit-Details: route_window=consumed, tenant_window=consumed
- Token accounting in billing snapshot shows ~1.8x expected token consumption during spike windows.

Why this is unusual / hypothesis:
- Customer changed route burst window to a shorter smoothing window at the same time tenant window was left unchanged; we hypothesize overlapping enforcement where the per-route limiter and tenant limiter both increment a shared token counter (shadow increments) for certain multipart/batch requests that are counted once at route layer and again at tenant layer when behind the dedicated gateway.
- HTTP/2 multiplexing and connection reuse may cause per-connection heuristics to misattribute request boundaries to the route layer, leading to double-accounting for the same effective token consumption.

Requested outcome from customer:
- Understand root cause and provide either a config change recommendation or a short-term mitigation to stop the 429s while preserving burst capacity for batch uploads.

Observed double increments in our token-accounting service for requests routed through the edge-proxy when route-level burst smoothing < tenant window length.

2026-03-11 13:20 - Platform Eng (Lina Kaur): Added hypothesis that the edge-proxy metrics emitter batches per-connection usage and then per-route emitter also samples per-request, resulting in duplicated increments when both emit within the same accounting tick. Linked internal PR to add de-dup stamps: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1428

2026-03-12 07:58 - Support (Marisol): Provided customer a temporary mitigation: increase route burst smoothing to match tenant window OR enable route-isolation flag on their dedicated pool. Customer to test and report back.

2026-03-12 16:05 - Veridian Eng (customer): Applied the temporary mitigation (route burst smoothing -> 60s to match tenant). Reports immediate drop in 429s from 4.2% -> 0.6% during a 20-minute smoke test.
2026-03-12 17:30 - Ethan Roberts (SRE): Marked as in-progress; scheduled follow-up to patch edge-proxy accounting and add an observability metric for duplicate-account events.
investigation_notes: Reproduced behavior in staging using a client that multiplexes short chat and large batch calls over HTTP/2. Root cause appears to be duplicate accounting across two layers: per-route limiter emits increments per logical request, while tenant-level emitter aggregates per-connection deltas. When route burst smoothing is narrower than tenant window, the same token consumption is observed in both emit windows and both increments are accepted by the central quota service. Edge-proxy PR 1428 adds a deduplication stamp (request-id + accounting-tick) and a toggle to prefer per-route accounting only for dedicated pools. Also observed minor correlation with multipart requests where body streaming causes accounting to be split across two emitter events.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation provided: customer updated route burst smoothing to equal tenant window and enabled route-isolation flag on dedicated pool. Immediate reduction in 429s observed. Medium-term fix: merged edge-proxy PR to add dedupe stamps and a config flag to prefer single-layer accounting for dedicated pools (PR linked above). Follow-up tasks: add alert for duplicate-account events, update dedicated pool runbook with guidance for route vs tenant window alignment, and include a console warning when a route-level smoothing window is smaller than tenant window for the same tenant.
next_steps: 1) Roll edge-proxy dedupe patch to canary (ENG-ops: deploy edge-proxy@canary to us-east-1)
2) Add console validation rule and warning UI (Product / Console team)
3) Create automated test that simulates HTTP/2 multiplexed accounting to prevent regressions
4) Customer follow-up in 48 hours to confirm full recovery under production load
